2607.20993.title: Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders
2607.20993.paper_summary: Large vision-language models are becoming increasingly dominant in 3D medical image interpretation, but we rarely know which internal units encode clinical findings or where that information lives in the representation. We first study this on a 3D chest vision-language model (Pillar-0) by probing its frozen vision embeddings. We show that (i) each radiological finding is encoded by a sparse set of ~10 vision-encoder channels that match full-feature classification performance and far exceed a zero-shot text prompting; (ii) turning off the channels tied to one finding, that finding's score collapses while unrelated labels stay stable; and (iii) the same sparse probe replicates on an architecturally unrelated 3D abdominal VLM (Merlin) suggesting a general property of frozen medical encoders. Our training-free concept channel probe (CCP) method, paired with a corpus-derived report template, outperforms published CT-CHAT on clinical efficacy and NLG metrics (F1 0.549 vs. 0.184; BLEU 0.483 vs. 0.373) at 22x lower latency. Our results provide a clear, reproducible characterization of how frozen medical encoders represent findings, demonstrating direct applicability across models.
2607.20993.paper_summary_zh: 大型視覺-語言模型在3D醫學影像解釋中變得越來越主導，但我們很少知道<i>哪些</i>內部單元編碼臨床發現或<i>這些</i>資訊在表示中位於何處。 我們首先在一個3D胸部視覺-語言模型（Pillar-0）上進行研究，通過探測其凍結的視覺嵌入。 我們顯示出 (i) 每個放射學發現都是由一組約10個稀疏的視覺編碼通道編碼，這些通道的性能與全特徵分類相匹配，並且遠遠超過零樣本文本提示； (ii) 關閉與某一發現相關的通道時，該發現的分數會崩潰，而無關的標籤保持穩定； (iii) 同樣的稀疏探測在一個架構上無關的3D腹部VLM（Merlin）上<i>重複</i>，這表明凍結醫學編碼器的一般特性。 我們的無需訓練的概念通道探測（CCP）方法，結合基於語料庫的報告模板，在臨床效能和自然語言生成指標上超越了已發表的CT-CHAT（F1 0.549對0.184；BLEU 0.483對0.373），且延遲降低了22倍。 我們的結果提供了一個清晰、可重複的特徵描述，說明凍結醫學編碼器如何表示發現，顯示出在各模型之間的直接適用性。
